overview: The Medford School Committee, meeting on school budget matters, evaluates departmental needs, federal grant allocations, capital facilities, and staffing priorities to construct and approve annual operating budget requests for Medford Public Schools. Across meetings held from May 2021 through May 2026, the committee has reviewed fiscal proposals spanning from FY22 to FY27 alongside central administration and city officials. Its work includes balancing fixed-cost inflation and collective bargaining obligations against municipal revenue constraints and expiring pandemic-relief funds. As of the May 2026 meeting, the committee approved the recommended preliminary FY27 operating budget featuring a $4.1 million base increase alongside $3.3 million in net reductions, while establishing a priority to restore a vacant inclusion specialist position when funding becomes available.

threads.name: Annual municipal budget requests and approvals
threads.summary: Across each fiscal year cycle, the committee evaluates district financial requirements and votes on formal operating budget requests submitted to municipal government. In June 2021, the committee approved an FY22 operating budget request of $68,221,865 to cover fixed costs and academic recovery initiatives. Subsequent requests included $72.4 million for FY23 in May 2022, $71,995,165 for FY24 in June 2023, and a level-service request of $79,399,774 for FY25 in May 2024. In March 2025, the committee approved an FY26 municipal budget request of $87,583,000, and most recently approved the recommended FY27 preliminary budget in May 2026.

threads.name: ESSER grant integration and pandemic relief funding
threads.summary: The district utilized one-time federal ESSER grant funding to support post-pandemic academic recovery while managing rising fixed operating costs. In May 2021, administration outlined using federal relief funds to address learning disruptions and support strategic staffing priorities. For the FY23 budget, administration developed a categorization system to separate recurring municipal operational needs from items funded through ESSER grants. By June 2023, committee discussions addressed the alignment of the FY24 budget with municipal targets while preparing for the federal funding cliff as ESSER grants expired.

threads.name: Student transportation policies and fees
threads.summary: The committee examined student transportation access and related fee structures to improve equity across the district. In May 2021, the committee passed a motion requiring the FY22 budget to eliminate out-of-pocket transportation costs for students living outside a two-mile radius who used MBTA passes. Administration subsequently worked on plans to expand yellow bus service for high school students while assessing vendor and safety data. In the FY23 budget, funding was allocated to maintain free MBTA passes for eligible students alongside student requests to address extracurricular user fees.

threads.name: Special Education and English Learner staffing
threads.summary: Budget reviews consistently focused on adjusting staffing levels for Special Education and English Learner (EL) programs to match enrollment demands. In May 2021, proposed priorities included adding an Evaluation Team Leader, expanding elementary specialized programs, and hiring EL-focused counseling staff. In May 2022, EL leadership requested four additional teachers to manage a record high enrollment of 577 newcomer students alongside requests for special education teachers and assistive technology. In May 2026, while approving FY27 budget reductions, the committee directed that reinstating a vacant inclusion specialist position be prioritized if additional funding arises.

threads.name: Curriculum, literacy, and academic interventions
threads.summary: The committee evaluated requests from academic departments for reading specialists, math interventionists, updated textbooks, and instructional technology. Early FY22 discussions focused on restoring middle school reading positions, adopting screening tools, and updating elementary math and adaptive literacy software. By May 2022, administration detailed partnerships with Hill for Literacy and a shift toward science of reading practices. In June 2023, the approved FY24 request explicitly incorporated funding for four elementary literacy coaches.

threads.name: Capital infrastructure and school facilities planning
threads.summary: The committee regularly separated major physical infrastructure repairs from operating budgets, shifting them to capital planning requests. In May 2021, priority infrastructure items included high school generator and transformer replacements, Curtis Tufts boiler repairs, and restroom renovations. In May 2022, operations presentations detailed ongoing facility maintenance needs, including high school repairs and McGlynn building leaks. In May 2024, the committee approved co-locating Curtis-Tufts School with Medford High School as part of the future high school building project and asked the MSBA feasibility study to evaluate CTE program expansions.

threads.name: Joint municipal coordination and financial planning
threads.summary: The committee collaborates with city officials to align budget schedules, evaluate municipal revenue forecasts, and plan for long-term obligations. In May 2022, discussions centered on aligning school requests with municipal appropriation timelines and potential shortfall contingencies. In March 2025, the City Council and School Committee held a joint meeting to establish joint procedures and review preliminary FY26 financial forecasts presented by CFO Bob Dickinson, which detailed available revenue projections and certified free cash balances.
